gaps.lead: It wasn't necessary for her to bring any food — there was plenty.
gaps.explanation: needn't have + participle = it wasn't necessary, but she did it.

gaps.lead: I have never heard such a ridiculous excuse.
gaps.explanation: Fronted 'never' forces inversion: Never have I heard…

gaps.lead: My grandfather had completely forgotten that he phoned me last night.
gaps.sentence: My grandfather didn't ___ phoning me last night.
gaps.explanation: 'Completely forgotten' becomes 'didn't have any recollection of'.

gaps.lead: Although he is remarkably rich, he lives very simply.
gaps.explanation: Although he may be rich → Rich as (he) may be — fronted adjective + as + may.

gaps.lead: Given that he has no experience, will Glyn be able to do this job?
gaps.sentence: Will Glyn's ___ his ability to do this job?
gaps.hint: no experience = lack of experience (noun subject)
gaps.explanation: The noun subject 'lack of experience' takes the verb 'affect'.

gaps.lead: My advice is to check the contract twice before signing.
gaps.sentence: You ___ the contract twice before signing.
gaps.explanation: had better + infinitive without 'to' = strong advice.
